Based on the clinical guidelines available, high-intensity statin therapy is recommended for primary prevention in adults aged 40-75 with LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL or diabetic individuals with additional risk factors. There is no routine recommendation to take aspirin daily for preventing cardiovascular events in healthy individuals of age 65 and older, except after a careful discussion regarding bleeding risks.

For primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in adults 40-70 years old, aspirin may be considered based on individual benefits versus risks; however, this is not a routine recommendation. It is important to consult with a healthcare provider for personalized preventive care advice considering the patient's specific health profile and risk factors.
